title: Schema for progressive shadow-first model trials with signal-driven rollback
creator: Sofia Alvarez
description: Create a product spec and delivery plan for a reusable A/B testing framework that supports a shadow-first canary path, staged exposure ramps, automated statistical checks (both sequential and fixed-sample), and deterministic auto-rollback triggers. This framework should integrate with the Console rollout UI and Runtime routing policies so teams can define experiments, control exposure, and get deterministic rollback when model quality or safety regressions are detected.
context: We have many ad-hoc experiments and manual rollouts across Hosted/Dedicated/Private customers. Engineering has requested a prescriptive experiment primitive that combines: (1) an easy experiment definition API, (2) shadow traffic plumbing for non-impactful signal collection, (3) staged exposure with backoff and guardrails, and (4) an automated rollback playbook tied to statistical tests and confidence thresholds.
goals: (1) Provide a declarative experiment manifest that covers shadow, canary, and full-traffic phases. (2) Implement exposure controller that enforces per-interval max/min ramps and immediate emergency cutover rules. (3) Provide a default set of sequential statistical checks (sequential t-test / proportion test, cumulative p-value correction) and an optional fixed-sample mode. (4) Wire alerts and automatic rollback policies that are auditable in the Console.
non_goals: This ticket does NOT include: new model training/eval tooling, advanced causal attribution for multi-variant experiments, or an external experiment analytics UI beyond Console widgets and alert hooks. It also does not implement custom experiment metrics ingestion pipelines (we will use existing metric exporters).
proposed_solution: Introduce an experiment manifest (yaml/json) with phases: shadow, canary, ramp, steady. Each phase defines sample fraction, metric families to monitor (latency/p95, error-rate, hallucination-score), and gating rules. The Runtime will support an 'experiment ID' header to tag requests and optionally route replicas as shadow duplicates. Console will get: (a) experiment creation form, (b) live exposure slider with safety override, (c) per-metric sequential-test visualizations and a single-click rollback button. Auto-rollback is an engine that monitors configured gates and performs a controlled revert (immediate or staged) with annotated audit log and optional rollback PR in GitHub for Private installs.
api_changes: Add ExperimentCreate/Update endpoints in Redwood API. Experiment manifest fields: name, description, model_variants (control, candidate), phases (ordered list), metrics (name, query, direction, threshold), stat_config (method: sequential|fixed, alpha, correction), rollback_policy (immediate|staged, notify_channels). SDKs get helpers to start/stop experiments and attach metadata to requests.
rollout_plan: 1) Start with internal infra teams and 2 pilot customers for 6 weeks; 2) Add default statistical checks and an emergency cutoff; 3) Iterate on Console UX based on pilot feedback; 4) Broader beta to 25 customers; 5) GA with docs and playbooks. Timeline: pilot start 2026-03-21, pilot end 2026-04-30, beta 2026-05-15, GA 2026-06-30.
exposure_control_details: Exposure controller enforces per-minute and per-hour absolute exposure caps, phase ramp percentages, and CPU/GPU-backed throughput ceilings. Supports cohort bucketing by user_id or request_hash; supports deterministic bucketing for repeatability. Shadow phase routes copies of requests to candidate without affecting response path; candidate outputs are logged and compared offline. On canary phase candidate receives live traffic fraction but also runs comparison checks against control.
statistical_checks: Default checks use sequential hypothesis testing (alpha-spending like O'Brien-Fleming) for primary metrics and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control for multi-metric scenarios. Implementations: sequential z-test for means with streaming variance estimator, sequential proportion test for error rates, and a robust median-based test for latency tails. Configurable look-bound and minimum sample thresholds. Optional fixed-sample mode supports classic t-tests with pre-specified N.
monitoring_and_alerts: Console dashboard shows cumulative estimates, confidence intervals, and earliest stopping time suggested by sequential test. Alerts: (1) soft warning when metric approaches threshold, (2) hard alarm when gating threshold crossed, (3) drift alert when candidate metric baseline shifts over window. Alerts can be routed to PagerDuty, Slack, or internal webhooks. Auto-rollback executes on hard alarm if rollback_policy.immediate == true.
dashboards: Pre-built Console panels: Experiment Summary, Per-Variant Time Series, Sequential Test Trace (alpha spent / p-value), Cohort Breakdown, and Safety Incidents log. Panels include links to raw logs in our observability stack and the ability to export CSV of per-request comparisons for offline audits.
runbook: Runbook steps: (1) Evaluate hard alarm payload and check primary metrics; (2) If auto-rollback triggered, verify rollback annotation and notify customer success; (3) If manual revert chosen, use Console rollback flow which creates a revert job in Runtime; (4) Postmortem: collect experiment logs, metric traces, and model inputs for failed examples and open follow-up PM/ENG tickets.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Experiment manifest schema reviewed and approved by infra and security. 2) Exposure controller enforces caps in staging. 3) Shadow traffic can be enabled with zero impact on response latency in staging. 4) Sequential tests run on streaming metric data and provide deterministic stop suggestions in >95% of test runs during pilot. 5) Auto-rollback executes and annotates events in audit log in staging.
success_metrics: Primary: reduction in time-to-safe-rollout (median time from pilot->GA) by 30% for pilot teams. Secondary: 50% fewer manual rollback incidents in first 3 months; adoption by 5 internal teams during pilot.
risks: Risk of false positives in sequential tests when traffic is highly nonstationary; risk that shadow replication increases request volume on model endpoints in Dedicated customers with tight quotas. Mitigations: conservative alpha spending, mandatory min-sample guards, and throttle knobs for shadow replication.
notes: We should align metric names with existing metric catalog to avoid duplicate instrumentation.
Consider an initial set of 3 out-of-the-box metrics: p95 latency, token error-rate (model exceptions), and hallucination-score (eval model).
